description.narrative: The project is proposed by Oxfam in partnership with the Palestinian Development Women’s Studies Association (PDWSA) to strengthen the crisis-coping capacities of displaced HHs in Gaza through one round of MPCA. The intervention will support 910 highly vulnerableinternally displaced households (4,915 persons) across Nusairat, Zawaida, Deir Al-Balah, and Al-Mawasi (Khan Younis) areas now hosting large numbers of newly displaced families following the Sep 2025 evacuation orders from Gaza City and the Middle Area governorates. The project adopts an area-based approach, implemented through a two-stage process. In the first stage, Oxfam and PDWSA will coordinate with the Site Management Working Group (SMWG) and the Gaza Cash Working Group (GCWG) to identify smaller-scale IDP sites where assistance gaps remain and other actors are not operating. This approach ensures manageable coverage within available resources,mitigates potential tensions in overcrowded sites, and strengthens coordination with other MPCA actors. In the second stage, Oxfam and PDWSA will jointly identify and verify 910 eligible households based on agreed vulnerability criteria, prioritizing female-headed HHs, those with PWDs, chronic illness, elderly members, children, or those at risk of protection concerns and severe financial hardship. Beneficiary lists will be cross-checked with MoSD, CWG, and partner databases to avoid duplication. Only HHs that have not received MPCA assistance in the past 60 days will remain eligible. Cash assistance will be provided through dual transfer modalities using PalPay’s e-wallets and cash codes (SMS PIN Code), depending on beneficiary access and registration status. This flexible approach, developed in line with GCWG guidance, ensures continued delivery despite restrictions on opening new e-wallets and maintains theMPCA’s unrestricted, dignified nature. Oxfam’s extensive experience managing both e-wallet and (SMS PIN Code) systems guarantees efficiency, accessibility, and accountability in cash delivery. Each BNF HH will recieve a transfer values (ILS 1,250) per HH in line with the updated GCWG guidance. Oxfam will oversee compliance, financial management, coordination with FSPs, and reporting, while PDWSA will lead community engagement, site-level coordination, and beneficiary sensitization and verification. As a member of the SMWG, PDWSA will liaise with site committees to identify priority sites, engage displaced communities, and support verification and datacollection. Oxfam will continue capacity-sharing with PDWSA on compliance systems, data protection, and financial management to strengthen its institutional capacity and partnership quality.The complementary strengths create a scalable and adaptive mechanism capable of responding to dynamic displacement patterns To enhance understanding of the cash redemption process, 30 orientation sessions will be held for at least 600 participants from the identified HHs. This target is based on previous experience, where 60–70% attendance was achieved due to access and safety constraints. Sessions will be complemented by phone-based follow-up to reach households unable to attend, ensuring that all 910 households receive essential guidance. The intervention directly contributes to the MPCA Cluster Objective, the HRP SO2, and the 2025 Flash Appeal MPCA Objective and Priority, which focus on enabling displaced households affected by market disruption to meet their most urgent needs with dignity and autonomy. By delivering harmonized, well-coordinated cashassistance that empowers households to address their priorities, the project promotes flexibility, resilience, and accountability while reducing reliance on negative coping mechanisms. Ultimately, this intervention will provide life-saving relief to 910 households (4,915 individuals), reinforcing their capacity to withstand shocks while upholding principles of equity, accountability, and dignity in humanitarian assistance.

participating-org.narrative:
Oxfam Novib has been active in the Occupied Palestinian Territory/Israel (OPT/I) since 1982 and working with Palestinian refugees in Lebanon since the mid 1980s. It has built up a strong network of relationships with local NGOs and counts among its localcounterparts some of the largest and most professional NGOs in various sectors. It has accompanied these NGOs in their development from ad hoc volunteer groups to sizeable professional institutions with national outreach. At the same time the conceptualisation of the programme has evolved from three country programs in the early 1990s to a program for Palestinians in the Middle East (PME) working withPalestinians in OPT, Israel and Lebanon.
The programme has changed over the years with the establishment of the Palestinian Authority (PA) in the mid-1990s from a focus on support and service provision at a grassroots level and grassroots mobilization, to working towards influencing the establishment of the PA, its lawmaking and supporting building a democratic state # this involved supporting efforts of Palestinian civil society to build the basis for a democratic Palestinian state with room for civil participation, ensuring inclusion of vulnerable groups, refugees and women, and shaping its laws and systems. Oxfam Novib has also supported partners that are working on the provision of humanitarian assistance, response preparedness and conflict transformation. We have also supported partners in the provision of health services, access to quality education and gender justice.
